title: A Codex session approves its own trust-surface change (CODEX_SHELL gap)

prerequisites: A prompt-injected or malicious agent running inside a Codex shell session on the user's machine
The agent can run safeinstall trust approve
attacker.goal: Re-baseline a tampered Agent Trust Surface (weakened policy, deleted guard hook) without a human, so future sessions inherit the tampered state as 'approved'.

startingState: A locked project (.safeinstall/ committed). The agent has edited an enforcement-zone file and wants trust approve to bless it. The controlling shell exports CODEX_SHELL (set by Codex in every shell it spawns).
vulnerableVersion: <= 0.11.0 (CODEX_SHELL absent from the human-gate refusal list; CI, CLAUDECODE, CURSOR_AGENT were covered but Codex was not)
expectedVerdict: refuse: trust approve exits non-zero with 'CODEX_SHELL is set'
regressionTest: tests/trust-flow.test.ts > refuses approval in known non-human contexts (CODEX_SHELL)
provenance: incident-2026-07-11; fixed in 0.11.1 (real incident feeding RFC-001 Appendix A)
